title: Trump order and USAGM actions sharply curtailed Voice of America operations
description_short: Trump order and USAGM actions sharply curtailed Voice of America operations
description_medium: Trump signed an executive order on March 14, 2025, directing USAGM to reduce operations to the minimum required by law. USAGM announced implementation the next day, saying the action would affect staff at USAGM, Voice of America and other outlets; it said most affected USAGM staff would be placed on paid administrative leave. The sources describe a sharp operational reduction, not a permanent abolition; the order was not issued by Marco Rubio.
description_long: On March 14, 2025, President Donald Trump signed an executive order directing the U.S. Agency for Global Media (USAGM) to reduce its operations to the minimum presence and functions required by law. The order calls for elimination of non-statutory components and functions only to the maximum extent consistent with applicable law. The next day, USAGM said it began implementation: the agency and the outlets it oversees would be reduced to statutory functions, with associated personnel reduced to the minimum presence and function required by law. The agency said the action would affect USAGM, Voice of America, the Office of Cuba Broadcasting and its grantees; it said most affected USAGM staff would begin paid administrative leave on March 15 and remain on leave until further notice. Reuters reported that the order sharply curtailed VOA and other agency operations. The documented action was taken under Trump’s order and implemented by USAGM, whose announcement includes Senior Adviser Kari Lake’s statement supporting implementation. These reports establish a major operational reduction, not permanent abolition of VOA or the asserted geopolitical effects, and do not attribute the order to Secretary of State Marco Rubio.
